about.title: Millbrae Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a faulty appliance, a car part that gives out on El Camino Real, or a tool that malfunctions on the job. Millbrae households deal with the same range of consumer goods, vehicles, and machinery as anywhere in San Mateo County, and when one of those products is defective in design, manufacture, or warning, the people who made or sold it can be held responsible under California's strict liability rules. That means an injured person generally doesn't need to prove anyone was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free service that connects Millbrae residents with independent attorneys who evaluate these cases and work on contingency. If a product hurt you, keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident — packaging, manuals, and all — and reach out so a qualified attorney can look at the details before evidence changes or gets discarded.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often proceed on a strict liability theory, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. An attorney can review your specific situation to determine which legal theory applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it in the same condition it was in when the incident happened, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. This evidence can be important for an attorney evaluating a claim, so avoid repairing, discarding, or altering it.

items.question: Why mention crash corridors like El Camino Real if this is about products?
items.answer: Some product liability claims in Millbrae involve defective vehicle parts — brakes, tires, or airbags — that fail on busy corridors like El Camino Real, US-101, or E Millbrae Avenue. If a vehicle component malfunctioned and contributed to a collision, that may be a product liability issue rather than a typical traffic case.
